text:
Henry Cho: pulling folks in for final PM review before we hit “publish + cut SDK releases” on the streaming/tool calling/structured output examples refresh. can everyone drop *blockers* here (or :white_check_mark: if none) so we can decide go/no-go by EOD PT? main things I’m looking for:
- terminology: “structured output” vs “JSON mode” vs “schema-constrained”
- model support matrix language (what we guarantee vs best-effort)
- any remaining compat gotchas w/ OpenAI-compat payload shapes

Nikhil Sharma: :eyes: on it. my current blockers list is 2 items:
1) support matrix copy still reads a bit too “guaranteed” for models where it’s best-effort. i want explicit language: “valid JSON is not guaranteed; validate + retry.”
2) ensure docs don’t imply we support partial JSON streaming parse as a product feature. we should recommend buffering until final + then validate.

Wei Chen: re (1) — agreed. in the structured output guide draft i have a table but it’s currently “Supported / Not supported”. i can change to “Schema-constrained output: Yes/Best-effort/No” + add footnote on fallback. will update in docs PR.

Elliot Price: terminology: we should be consistent across:
- streaming guide
- tool calling guide
- structured output guide
- quickstarts README

proposal from docs side:
- public term: **Structured output (JSON Schema)**
- avoid “JSON mode” (too vendor-coded)
- use “schema-constrained” only as explanatory adjective, not headline term

Kira Thompson: +1. also aligns w/ Confluence DX standards draft. we can add a one-liner definition for each term in the “Known pitfalls” section so support can link it.

Ibrahim Khan: on compat gotchas: biggest one is examples accidentally mixing two shapes:
- tool calls as an array on message vs tool call deltas in stream
- tool_result message role naming

the canonical pattern we’re enforcing in examples matches the ADR payload shape (keep tool calls inside assistant message, then send tool-result messages). but docs need a callout: “payloads may differ from OpenAI; see compat table.”

Brian Murphy: i reviewed the example snippets in the docs PR earlier today. one thing to fix: the streaming loop should *not* assume `tool_call.arguments` is complete in any given delta. it should explicitly append args fragments until we see the final tool_call event. otherwise we’ll keep getting SUP-18421 style reports.

Monica Patel: python SDK side is good. we added the “args accumulation” helper in the sample + golden transcript test. but agree docs should show that pattern (even if abbreviated) so people don’t copy the naive version.

Markus Klein: from Solutions Eng: launch blocker is mostly wording + expectation management. prospects keep asking “do you guarantee valid JSON always?” we need a crisp answer:
- “we support schema-constrained output on select models; still validate; for strict workflows implement retry + fallback.”

also: in the tool calling page, the “parallel tool calls” section needs a sentence that Redwood may emit calls in any order and you should match by id/name, not array index.

Henry Cho: great. let’s track as blockers:
A) structured output support matrix copy (Yes/Best-effort/No + explicit validate/retry)
B) docs snippet shows partial tool args handling
C) parallel tool calls ordering caveat

Nikhil Sharma: +1. also want consistent phrasing on “guarantee” vs “aim”. suggestion:
- use “guarantee” only when we actually enforce via constrained decoding
- otherwise say “best-effort; validate client-side”

Wei Chen: ack. i’ll update the matrix + copy. will also add an “Implementation notes” callout box:
- buffer streamed deltas
- validate final JSON
- retry w/ “return ONLY valid JSON matching this schema” system nudge

Elliot Price: for B) i can update the tool calling doc snippet. we don’t need to show full accumulator implementation but we can show:
- `argsBuffer[toolCallId] += delta`
- “don’t parse until done”

Alex Martinez: checking in. i’m fine holding launch for 24h if needed to get the copy right. support load from misleading “guaranteed JSON” language will erase any win from shipping early.

Connor O'Brien: from releases side: if docs updates land today by ~5pm PT, we can still cut SDK patch releases tomorrow morning and do comms in #announcements after. if it slips, we should move the release window and avoid a docs/SDK mismatch.

Brian Murphy: quick nit: docs should say “JSON Schema (draft-07 compatible subset)” or whatever we actually support. otherwise people will paste in advanced schema keywords and file tickets.

Wei Chen: good call. i’ll add a line: “Examples use a draft-07 compatible subset; avoid unevaluatedProperties/if-then-else; see guidance.” (keeping it short).

Kira Thompson: i can mirror that into the internal standards page later, but for launch the public doc is the priority.

Monica Patel: on the SDK side, TS types were updated to avoid mismatch on tool result shape. but if docs show `tool_result` as a string vs object we’ll regress confusion. pls ensure the example shows a consistent tool result message shape across languages.

Ibrahim Khan: +1. parity guideline is:
- tool definition includes `name`, `description`, `parameters` (JSON schema)
- tool result message includes `tool_call_id` and `content` (stringified JSON ok, but be consistent)

if docs show “result: {…}” in one and “content: …” in another, we’re back to square one.

Elliot Price: noted. i’ll check code tabs; they *must* match across languages. i’ll ping Design if the tab UI truncates lines again.

Henry Cho: status check — are we comfortable making A/B/C the last blockers? anything else?

Markus Klein: only other thing: add a one-liner in streaming guide about disconnect/retry: “retry from scratch; idempotency key recommended; don’t attempt to resume partial JSON.” not a blocker but would be nice.

Nikhil Sharma: not a blocker for me. A/B/C are the big ones.

Wei Chen: i can add that line quickly while touching the page.

Connor O'Brien: :thumbsup: as long as we don’t change API semantics, just wording.

Henry Cho: ok. action items:
- Wei: update model support matrix + “validate/retry” copy + schema subset note + disconnect/retry line
- Elliot: update tool calling snippet to show args accumulation + parallel ordering caveat + ensure code tabs consistent tool result shape
- Brian/Ibrahim: quick re-review once those changes are up

EOD target: docs PR updates ready for final signoff by 4:30pm PT.

Wei Chen: on it. will post links here when pushed.

Elliot Price: same.

Brian Murphy: will re-review.

Ibrahim Khan: will re-review.

Alex Martinez: thanks all. :white_check_mark: once the copy is precise, i’m good to approve launch.

Henry Cho: perfect. holding go/no-go until reviewers confirm.

—

Wei Chen: pushed updates to structured output guide draft (matrix + language + schema subset). also added explicit “buffer until final, then validate”. pls review.

Elliot Price: updated tool calling page snippet w/ args accumulation note + added warning that tool calls may arrive out of order; match by id. also normalized tool-result message shape across tabs.

Brian Murphy: reviewed. B) fixed; snippet now explicitly accumulates args and only parses at end. :thumbsup:

Ibrahim Khan: reviewed. C) included. tool result shape looks consistent across tabs. :thumbsup:

Nikhil Sharma: reviewed the matrix copy. A) looks good — “Yes / Best-effort / No” + validate/retry is explicit. terminology is consistent (“Structured output (JSON Schema)”). :white_check_mark:

Connor O'Brien: cool. with this, release train is unblocked from my side.

Henry Cho: awesome. marking blockers cleared. GO for launch pending merge + publish. :rocket: (and pls keep an eye on support tickets for JSON validity confusion next week)
